# SEC TRIBUNAL — PROSECUTION'S BEAR CASE
## In re: INTEL CORP (INTC, CIK 0000050863)

Your Honors, the People present the following charges against the defendant, supported entirely by the defendant's own sworn filings [Exhibit A].

---

**CHARGE 1 — Structural Revenue Collapse: One-Third of the Business Erased in Four Years**

The defendant's annual revenue fell from **$79.02B in FY2021 to $52.85B in FY2025** — a cumulative decline of roughly 33%, with *every single fiscal year* negative: -20.2% (FY2022), -14.0% (FY2023), -2.1% (FY2024), and -0.5% (FY2025) [Exhibit A]. Four consecutive years of shrinkage is not a cycle; it is secular decay. The recent quarterly uptick (25.4% YoY in Q ended 2026-06-27) merely lifts revenue back toward levels the defendant abandoned years ago.

**CHARGE 2 — Gross Margin Destruction of Historic Proportions**

Gross margin was cut nearly in half: **55.4% in FY2021 to 32.7% in FY2024**, recovering only to 34.8% in FY2025 [Exhibit A]. Gross profit dollars collapsed from **$43.81B (FY2021) to $18.38B (FY2025)** — a loss of over $25B in annual gross profit. Even the "improved" recent quarters (40.4% in Q ended 2026-06-27) remain some 15 points below the defendant's FY2021 standard. This is a business whose pricing power and cost structure have been fundamentally impaired.

**CHARGE 3 — The Core Business Loses Money: Persistent Operating Losses**

Operating income cratered from **$19.46B (FY2021)** to **$93.0M (FY2023)**, then to an operating **loss of $11.68B (FY2024)** and a further **loss of $2.21B (FY2025)** [Exhibit A]. The instability continues quarterly: -$3.18B (Q ended 2025-06-28) and -$3.14B (Q ended 2026-03-28), with operating margin swinging from -24.7% to +11.1% within a year. Two consecutive fiscal years of negative operating income means the enterprise, at its core, destroys value.

**CHARGE 4 — Net Losses Culminating in a Catastrophic Recent Quarter**

Net income fell from **$19.87B (FY2021)** to **-$18.76B (FY2024)** and **-$267.0M (FY2025)** [Exhibit A]. Most damning: in the quarter ended 2026-06-27, the defendant reported a **net loss of $11.03B** — a net margin of **-68.4%** — even as it posted positive operating income of $1.80B. In the same quarter, stockholders' equity plunged from **$111.39B (2026-03-28) to $87.54B**, a destruction of nearly $24B of equity in a single quarter [Exhibit A].

**CHARGE 5 — Rising Leverage on a Weakened Balance Sheet**

Long-term debt climbed from **$33.51B (FY2021) to $46.98B (FY2023)**, and jumped again from **$43.03B (2026-03-28) to $48.55B (2026-06-27)** — a $5.5B increase in one quarter, precisely as equity collapsed. The result: **LT-debt/equity surged from 0.35 (FY2021) to 0.55 (2026-06-27)** [Exhibit A]. Interest expense had already risen from $496.0M (FY2022) to $878.0M (FY2023). The defendant is borrowing more while earning less.

**CHARGE 6 — Cash Generation Gutted and Innovation Spending in Retreat**

Operating cash flow collapsed from **$29.46B (FY2021) to $8.29B (FY2024)** — a 72% decline — with only a modest recovery to $9.70B (FY2025) [Exhibit A]. Meanwhile, R&D expense — the lifeblood of a semiconductor company — was cut from **$16.55B (FY2024) to $13.77B (FY2025)**, a ~17% reduction, with quarterly R&D falling from $3.68B (Q ended 2025-06-28) to $3.37B (Q ended 2026-06-27). The defendant is mortgaging its future to survive its present.

---

**CONCLUSION**

The record shows a company that has lost a third of its revenue, half its gross margin, all of its operating profitability, and $24B of equity in a single recent quarter — while leverage rises to its highest level in the record (0.55) and R&D investment retreats. The People rest.

# SEC TRIBUNAL — DEFENSE'S REBUTTAL
## In re: INTEL CORP (INTC) — Peer benchmark: ADVANCED MICRO DEVICES (AMD)

Your Honors, the Defense does not ask the Tribunal to ignore my client's difficult years. We ask only that the record be read completely — including the trajectory of the most recent five quarters and the structural differences between my client and its fabless competitor — before judgment is rendered.

---

**REBUTTAL TO CHARGE 1 — Revenue: The Decline Has Ended and Reversed**

The Defense concedes the historical decline: $79.02B (FY2021) to $52.85B (FY2025) is real, and unlike the broader industry-wide 2022–2023 correction — which touched even AMD, whose revenue fell -3.9% in FY2023 [Exhibit B] — most of my client's decline reflects company-specific share loss. We will not pretend otherwise.

But the prosecution's own timeline stops where the recovery begins. The last two annual declines were -2.1% and -0.5% — statistical flatness, not "collapse" [Exhibit A]. And the most recent quarters show **acceleration**: revenue of $13.58B (+7.2% YoY, Q ended 2026-03-28) and **$16.13B (+25.4% YoY, Q ended 2026-06-27)** — the highest quarterly revenue anywhere in the quarterly record [Exhibit A]. A "structural collapse" does not produce 25% growth. The bleeding has stopped; the direction has changed.

---

**REBUTTAL TO CHARGE 2 — Gross Margin: Five Consecutive Data Points of Recovery, and a False Comparison**

Quarterly gross margin, in sequence, since the trough: 27.5% → 38.2% → 39.4% → **40.4%** (Q ended 2026-06-27) [Exhibit A]. Annual gross margin rose from 32.7% (FY2024) to 34.8% (FY2025), and gross profit *dollars* grew year-over-year for the first time in the record: $17.34B → $18.38B [Exhibit A].

As for the comparison to FY2021's 55.4%: the prosecution invites the Tribunal to benchmark an integrated manufacturer building out its own fabrication capacity against a **fabless** peer. AMD carries roughly $2.35B of long-term debt and $84.46B of total assets [Exhibit B]; my client carries **$202.44B of total assets** [Exhibit A] — the weight of physical manufacturing. Fab construction and ramp costs flow directly through cost of sales before those fabs generate revenue at scale. That is a deliberate, capital-intensive investment in manufacturing capacity — a strategic asset AMD does not attempt to own — not evidence of "fundamentally impaired" pricing power.

---

**REBUTTAL TO CHARGE 3 — Operating Losses: An 81% Improvement, Then a Return to Profit**

The operating loss narrowed from **-$11.68B (FY2024) to -$2.21B (FY2025)** — an improvement of roughly $9.5B in one year [Exhibit A]. The most recent quarter posted operating income of **+$1.80B, an 11.1% operating margin** — the strongest quarterly operating result in the entire record [Exhibit A].

The prosecution cites the -$3.14B quarter (2026-03-28) as evidence of instability. But note: that same quarter carried a **39.4% gross margin and 7.2% revenue growth** [Exhibit A]. Healthy gross economics combined with a large operating loss is the signature of concentrated period charges — restructuring — not of a core business that "destroys value." Even the peer was not immune to lumpy quarters: AMD itself posted an operating **loss** of -$134.0M in the quarter ended 2025-06-28 [Exhibit B].

---

**REBUTTAL TO CHARGE 4 — The $11.03B Net Loss: A Below-the-Line Event, Not an Operating Failure**

The prosecution's "most damning" exhibit actually proves the Defense's case. In the quarter ended 2026-06-27, my client earned **+$1.80B in operating income** while reporting a -$11.03B net loss [Exhibit A]. By definition, the entire loss arose *below the operating line* — non-operating, non-recurring items. The concurrent equity decline from $111.39B to $87.54B is consistent with a one-time balance-sheet charge, not with the operations of the business, which were profitable that very quarter.

The Defense also directs the Tribunal to the annual trend the prosecution buried: net income improved from **-$18.76B (FY2024) to -$267.0M (FY2025)** — a 98%+ reduction in losses [Exhibit A] — and the company posted a quarterly net profit of **+$4.06B** (Q ended 2025-09-27) [Exhibit A].

---

**REBUTTAL TO CHARGE 5 — Leverage: Elevated, Not Distressed**

Facts the prosecution omitted: long-term debt actually **declined** from $46.98B (FY2023) to $44.09B (2025-12-27), and stood at $43.03B as recently as 2026-03-28 [Exhibit A]. Cash rose from **$8.25B (FY2024) to $12.87B** in the latest quarter, having reached $17.25B the quarter prior [Exhibit A]. A company hoarding rising cash while holding debt roughly flat over two years is managing its balance sheet, not drowning under it.

The 0.55 debt/equity ratio in the latest quarter is elevated — but it spiked primarily because the *denominator* fell on the one-time charge addressed in Charge 4, not because of reckless borrowing. And in absolute terms, $48.55B of debt against $87.54B of equity and $202.44B of assets [Exhibit A] is a leveraged-but-solvent industrial balance sheet. Yes, AMD runs at 0.03 [Exhibit B] — because AMD builds no fabs. Comparing the leverage of a company constructing national-scale manufacturing capacity to a fabless designer is not evidence; it is a category error.

---

**REBUTTAL TO CHARGE 6 — Cash Flow and R&D: Still Out-Generating and Out-Spending the Peer**

Operating cash flow was **positive in every single period on the record** — through the worst years [Exhibit A]. It grew from $8.29B (FY2024) to $9.70B (FY2025), and the latest reported quarter shows $1.10B versus $813M a year earlier, a ~35% increase [Exhibit A]. Critically: my client's FY2025 operating cash flow of **$9.70B exceeds AMD's $7.71B** [Exhibit B] — the "gutted" defendant still generates more operating cash than the prosecution's star witness.

On R&D: yes, spending fell from $16.55B to $13.77B [Exhibit A]. But $13.77B remains **~70% more than AMD's $8.09B** [Exhibit B], and represents roughly 26% of my client's revenue versus AMD's roughly 23% ($8.09B / $34.64B) [Exhibits A, B]. A company "mortgaging its future" does not maintain the larger R&D budget in the industry comparison, in both dollars and intensity, while restructuring.

---

**HONEST CONCESSIONS**

The Defense will not insult the Tribunal:
1. **Charge 1's history is largely valid.** AMD grew revenue 43.6% (FY2022) and 34.3% (FY2025) while my client shrank [Exhibit B]. This was share loss, not merely an industry cycle. Our defense rests on the reversal, not on denial of the decline.
2. **The competitive gap remains wide.** AMD's latest quarter: 53.8% gross margin, 17.3% operating margin, 50.1% revenue growth [Exhibit B]. My client is recovering, not yet winning.
3. **FY2024 was genuinely catastrophic**, and the Q2-2026 equity destruction is real economic loss to shareholders, whatever its accounting character.

---

**CONCLUSION**

The prosecution has convicted the Intel of 2022–2024. The company before this Tribunal in 2026 shows 25.4% revenue growth, four consecutive quarters of gross-margin expansion to 40.4%, record quarterly operating income of $1.80B, rising cash of $12.87B, positive operating cash flow in every period, and an R&D budget that still dwarfs its chief competitor's [Exhibits A, B]. The charges describe the patient's history. The vital signs describe recovery. The Defense rests.
rebuttal:
# SEC TRIBUNAL — PROSECUTION'S REBUTTAL
## In re: INTEL CORP (INTC)

Your Honors, three points, and the record of concessions.

---

**FOR THE RECORD — Defense Concessions.** The defense has conceded on the record: (1) the FY2021–FY2025 revenue decline was *company-specific share loss*, not industry cycle; (2) FY2024 was "genuinely catastrophic"; and (3) the Q2-2026 destruction of shareholder equity "is real economic loss to shareholders, whatever its accounting character." Charge 1's historical substance and the equity destruction in Charge 4 stand admitted. The People do not contest the recent revenue reacceleration or the continuity of positive operating cash flow; we rest those charges on the conceded history.

**FIRST — The "one-time, below-the-line" theory of the $11.03B loss is speculation contradicted by the balance sheet.** Nothing in Exhibit A identifies that loss as non-recurring; the defense invented that characterization. What Exhibit A *does* show for that single quarter: equity fell $23.85B ($111.39B → $87.54B), long-term debt **rose $5.52B** ($43.03B → $48.55B), and cash **fell $4.38B** ($17.25B → $12.87B). A benign paper charge does not require $5.5B of fresh borrowing and a $4.4B cash drawdown in the same ninety days. And the defense's "one-time" framing collapses under repetition: -$18.76B (FY2024), then -$821M, -$2.92B, -$3.73B, and -$11.03B across four of the last six reported quarterly results [Exhibit A]. A charge that recurs every few quarters is not "one-time." It is the business.

**SECOND — The "record quarter" does not rescue the operating record; arithmetic does not permit it.** Sum the five recent quarters the defense celebrates: -$301M, -$3.18B, +$683M, -$3.14B, +$1.80B — a **cumulative operating loss of roughly $4.14B** across the very period the defense calls a recovery [Exhibit A]. Three of five quarters were operating losses. And the defense's own explanation for the -$3.14B quarter — "concentrated restructuring charges" — appears nowhere in Exhibit A; it is another unsupported assertion. What the exhibit *does* show is that in that quarter the company generated $5.35B of gross profit and still lost $3.14B at the operating line — meaning roughly $8.5B of operating costs consumed the quarter. One good quarter against that backdrop is a data point, not an acquittal.

**THIRD — "Elevated, not distressed" ignores the direction of travel in the most recent filing.** The defense's leverage narrative — debt flat, cash rising — was true through 2026-03-28 and expired immediately thereafter. The latest quarter shows debt at its **highest level in the entire record ($48.55B)**, cash falling, and LT-debt/equity at its **worst level in the record (0.55)**, up from 0.35 in FY2021 [Exhibit A]. The defense says the ratio spiked "primarily" because equity fell. Not so: *both* terms moved against the defendant — the numerator rose $5.5B while the denominator fell $23.85B. And this leverage is carried by a company whose interest expense had already risen 77% ($496M → $878M) between FY2022 and FY2023, with operating income cumulatively negative since. Borrowing more, at higher cost, while the core operation runs at a loss — that is the definition of the charge.

---

The defense asks the Tribunal to weigh one strong quarter against two conceded catastrophic years, three operating losses in five quarters, a recurring pattern of multi-billion-dollar net losses, and record leverage. The People submit the scale does not balance. The prosecution rests.

verdict.summary: Intel stands accused of secular revenue decay, margin destruction, persistent operating and net losses, rising leverage, and gutted cash generation, based on its own filings. The defense concedes the 2021–2024 damage but argues the most recent quarters show a genuine turnaround (25.4% revenue growth, 40.4% gross margin, record $1.80B operating income). The tribunal finds the historical damage and recent equity destruction largely proven, but the defense successfully rebutted the claims of ongoing cash-flow failure and terminal decline, producing a mixed verdict on a distressed-but-recovering enterprise.

charges.charge: Revenue collapsed 33% from $79.02B (FY2021) to $52.85B (FY2025) with four consecutive years of decline, constituting secular decay.
charges.rebuttal: The decline has ended and reversed, with the last two annual declines nearly flat (-2.1%, -0.5%) and the latest quarter posting record revenue of $16.13B at +25.4% YoY growth.

charges.charge: Gross margin was cut from 55.4% (FY2021) to 32.7% (FY2024), a loss of over $25B in annual gross profit, evidencing impaired pricing power.
charges.rebuttal: Margins have recovered for four consecutive quarters to 40.4%, gross profit dollars grew YoY for the first time, and comparing an integrated manufacturer ramping fabs to fabless AMD is a category error.

charges.charge: The core business destroys value, with operating losses of -$11.68B (FY2024) and -$2.21B (FY2025) and continued quarterly instability.
charges.rebuttal: The FY2025 loss narrowed by roughly $9.5B and the latest quarter posted record operating income of +$1.80B (11.1% margin), with interim losses attributable to restructuring.

charges.charge: Net losses culminated in a catastrophic -$11.03B quarter (-68.4% margin) that destroyed nearly $24B of stockholders' equity in ninety days.
charges.rebuttal: The loss arose entirely below a profitable operating line (+$1.80B), indicating a one-time non-operating charge rather than an operating failure.

charges.charge: Long-term debt hit a record $48.55B while equity collapsed, driving LT-debt/equity to a record 0.55 as interest expense rose 77%.
charges.rebuttal: Debt was roughly flat or declining until the latest quarter, cash rose from $8.25B to $12.87B, and $48.55B of debt against $202.44B of assets is leveraged but solvent for a fab-building manufacturer.

charges.charge: Operating cash flow collapsed 72% from $29.46B (FY2021) to $8.29B (FY2024) while R&D was cut 17%, mortgaging the future.
charges.rebuttal: Operating cash flow was positive in every single period, grew to $9.70B in FY2025 (exceeding AMD's $7.71B), and R&D of $13.77B remains ~70% larger than AMD's in dollars and higher in intensity.

verdict.recommendation: Intel is a distressed turnaround, not a healthy investment. The conceded facts — company-specific share loss, a catastrophic FY2024, three operating losses in the last five quarters, a recurring pattern of multi-billion-dollar net losses culminating in $24B of equity destruction, and record leverage of 0.55 debt/equity taken on at rising cost — outweigh a single strong quarter. However, the recovery signals are real: 25.4% revenue growth, four straight quarters of gross-margin expansion to 40.4%, record quarterly operating income, uninterrupted positive operating cash flow, and R&D spending that still exceeds its chief rival's. An investor should treat INTC as a high-risk speculative recovery position sized accordingly, and should require at least two to three consecutive quarters of sustained operating profitability, clarity on the source and recurrence of the below-the-line losses, and stabilization of debt and equity before considering it investable on fundamentals.
